subtitulo: Past tense that isn't about the past
descripcion: After *I wish*, *if only* and *it's time*, English uses a past tense to talk about the present. *I wish I knew* is about now, not about yesterday. It looks like a mistake and it is the rule. This is the structure of regret, frustration and wanting things to be different — which makes it one of the most emotionally useful things at B2.

filas: He talks as if he **knew** everything.
cuadroReferencia.notaPie: **Were, not was,** in careful English: I wish I **were** there. Was is very common in speech and accepted, but were is the safe choice in writing.

ejemplos.texto: *I wish we lived closer to my parents.*
*If only I had said something at the time.*
*It's time we talked about it properly.*

notas: *I wish* + *would* cannot be about yourself. *I wish I would stop* is wrong; you control that, so it is *I wish I could stop*.
*It's time* with an infinitive is different and simpler: *It's time to go* is neutral. *It's time we went* carries a mild reproach.
*I'd rather* takes a bare infinitive for yourself (*I'd rather go*) and a past tense for someone else (*I'd rather you went*).

contraste.es: Spanish uses the subjunctive here — ojalá tuviera más tiempo — and the subjunctive is a distinct verb form. English has no separate subjunctive left, so it borrows the past tense. The logic is the same: an unreal form for an unreal situation.
contraste.de: German uses the Konjunktiv II (Ich wünschte, ich hätte mehr Zeit), and hätte maps neatly onto the English past had. The traps are I wish I would have… and it's time with the present tense, copied from German es wird Zeit, dass wir gehen (it's time we went).
contraste.it: Italian uses the congiuntivo imperfetto (magari avessi più tempo), which maps well onto the English past (I wish I had more time). After è ora che, colloquial Italian often uses the present (è ora che andiamo), which leads to it's time we go instead of it's time we went.
contraste.fr: French si seulement + imparfait (si seulement j'avais plus de temps) maps exactly onto if only I had. For wish, French uses j'aimerais or je voudrais, which leads to I would like to have more time instead of I wish I had; after il est temps que French uses the subjunctive present, which can produce it's time we go.
contraste.pt: Portuguese expresses the wish with quem me dera (European) or tomara que (Brazilian) plus the subjunctive, which maps well onto I wish I had. After já é hora, Portuguese often uses a personal infinitive (já é hora de irmos), which corresponds well to it's time for us to go.

errores: *I wish I have more time* — the present tense breaks the structure.
*I wish he will listen* — after *wish*, *would*, never *will*.
*I wish I would stop smoking* — use *could* for yourself.
*It's time we talk* — needs the past form, *talked*.

es: *ojalá* + present subjunctive rendered with *wish*: *I wish you have a good trip* instead of *I hope you have a good trip*.
de: *Ich wünsche mir, dass er kommt* rendered as *I wish he comes* instead of *I hope he comes* or *I wish he would come*.
it: *spero che* confused with *wish*: *I wish you are well* instead of *I hope you are well*.
fr: *je souhaite que tu viennes* rendered as *I wish you come* instead of *I hope you come* or *I'd like you to come*.
pt: *tomara que* rendered with *wish*: *I wish you have fun* instead of *I hope you have fun*.

mision.consigna: Write about a relationship you wish were different: with a relative, a friend, someone you lost touch with.
requisitos: at least three *I wish* with the past simple; two with the past perfect; one *I wish … would* about someone else; one *if only*; one *it's time*

microtareas.texto: Write five things you'd like to be different right now. Start each with *I wish*.
Turn three of them into past regrets with the past perfect.
Record 90 seconds: *What do you wish you had done differently?*

autochequeo: Is the verb after every *I wish* in a past form?
Did I use *would* about myself by mistake?
Does *it's time* take a past tense?
Did I use *were* rather than *was* in writing?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the unreal past: *wish*, *if only*, *it's time*, *I'd rather*, *as if*. (1) Check the tense after each one. (2) Flag any *would* used about the speaker. (3) Flag *was* where careful English wants *were*. (4) Say where a past perfect would have been more accurate than a past simple. Do not correct anything else.
